title: Library Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $2,500,000 for the purpose of purchasing materials and resources for libraries within Bernalillo County, New Mexico, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Public Safety Facilities, Fleet and Other County Buildings Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $8,900,000 for the purpose of acquiring property, planning, designing, upgrading, constructing, remodeling, purchasing, furnishing, equipping, repairing and otherwise improving, County facilities and fleet, including but not limited to health and public safety facilities, fire station and law enforcement facilities, jail and detention center facilities, courthouse facilities, youth and family service center and learning facilities, visitors center facilities, necessary redevelopment of facilities, replacement of fleet vehicles and heavy equipment, and construction and improvements required by the Americans with Disabilities Act, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Parks and Recreation Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $20,384,920 for the purpose of acquiring property, planning, designing, upgrading, constructing, remodeling, furnishing, equipping, repairing and otherwise improving park and recreational facilities within the County, including but not limited to parks, aquatic centers, community centers, playgrounds, ball fields, open spaces, cultural and educational facilities, community recreation centers and pools, and necessary redevelopment of facilities, and construction and improvements required by the Americans with Disabilities Act, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Transportation Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $6,215,080 for the purpose of acquiring property, planning, designing, upgrading, constructing, rehabilitating, furnishing, equipping, repairing and otherwise improving transportation facilities within the County, including but not limited to roads, non-motor vehicle pathways, bridges, traffic calming facilities, bike lanes, trails, sidewalks, transit improvements, paving, landscaping, traffic signals and other street improvements, and necessary construction and improvements required by the Americans with Disabilities Act, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Storm Drainage and Utilities Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $1,000,000 for the purpose of acquiring property, planning, designing, upgrading, constructing, rehabilitating, equipping, repairing and otherwise improving drainage and utility infrastructure, including but not limited to storm sewer and drainage, wastewater, water and drainage systems and facilities within Bernalillo County, New Mexico, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Public Housing Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $6,000,000 for the purpose of acquiring property, planning, designing, upgrading, constructing, remodeling, rehabilitating, furnishing, equipping, repairing and otherwise improving housing facilities within the County, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Public Safety Gross Receipts Tax Dedication Update
text: Shall the City of Albuquerque amend the Public Safety Gross Receipts Tax to divide funds amongst updated city services? The money would be divided as follows: Police 35%; Fire 38%; Albuquerque Community Safety 8%; Health, Housing, and Homelessness 8%; Prisoner Transport 6%; and Code Enforcement 5%. This would not increase the tax rate.

title: Performing Arts Center Funding Requirement
text: Shall the Charter of the City of Albuquerque be amended to repeal Article XI, Section 7, which requires voter approval before the City may appropriate more than $10 million for a performing arts center so that future funding of any amount would no longer require a separate vote?

title: Albuquerque Community Safety (ACS) Chief Appointment
text: Shall the Charter of the City of Albuquerque be amended to designate the Director of Albuquerque Community Safety as the "ACS Chief" and require that this position be appointed by the Mayor with the advice and consent of the City Council, subject to the same confirmation, employment agreement, and removal terms currently applied to the Police Chief and Fire Chief?

place: Albuquerque Metropolitan Arroyo Flood Control Authority
title: General Obligation Flood Control Bonds
text: Shall the Albuquerque Metropolitan Arroyo Flood Control Authority be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds in principal amount- not exceeding $30,000 000 for the extension betterment, alteration, reconstruction, repair and other improvements of the Authority's flood control system?

title: Fire Improvement Bonds
text: Bonds of the City of Rogers in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $32,750,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of fire department facilities, equipment and apparatus and parking, furnishings, drainage, flood control, lighting, road, and utility improvements therefor and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 1% local sales and use tax within the City.

title: Police Improvement Bonds
text: Bonds of the City of Rogers in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $20,750,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of police department facilities, equipment and apparatus and parking, furnishings, drainage, flood control, lighting, road, and utility improvements therefor and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 1% local sales and use tax within the City.

title: Animal Services Improvement Bonds
text: Bonds of the City of Rogers in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $8,750,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of animal services facilities, equipment and apparatus and parking, furnishings, drainage, flood control, lighting, road, and utility improvements therefor and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 1% local sales and use tax within the City.

title: Refunding Bonds
text: Bonds of the City of Rogers in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $118,000,000 for the purpose of refunding the City's outstanding Sales and Use Tax Bonds, Improvement Series 2018B and Sales and Use Tax Bonds, Series 2022 and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 1% local sales and use tax within the City.

title: Street Improvement Bonds
text: Bonds of the City of Rogers in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $195,500,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of streets, roads, trails and bridges, including any curb, gutter, drainage, flood control and other related improvements, equipment and land acquisition to accomplish such improvements, and street lighting, utility adjustments, sidewalks and traffic signals related thereto and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 1% local sales and use tax within the City.

title: Park and Recreational Improvement Bonds
text: Bonds of the City of Rogers in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $81,500,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of park and recreational facilities and improvements and any necessary land acquisition and parking, furnishings, equipment, drainage, flood control, lighting, road, trail, and utility improvements therefor and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 1% local sales and use tax within the City.

title: City of Little Flock Special Election
text: An ordinance levying an additional one percent (1%) Sales and Compensating Use Tax within the City of Little Flock, Arkansas, to be used for general operational purposes; prescribing other matters relating to the levy; and for other purposes.

title: City of Siloam Springs Special Election: Bonds and Tax
text: Bonds of the City of Siloam Springs in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $55,000,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of extensions, betterments and improvements to the City's wastewater facilities, including particularly, without limitation, wastewater treatment plant and sewer collection infrastructure, and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 0.625% local sales and use tax within the City. If the bonds are approved, there will be levied within the City a 0.625% local sales and use tax (the "Bond Tax"), the net collections of which remaining after deduction of the administrative charges of the State of Arkansas and required rebates will be used solely to retire or pay obligations with respect to the bonds in accordance with Amendment No. 62 to the Arkansas Constitution. The Bond Tax will expire after the bonds have been paid or provision is made therefor in accordance with Arkansas statutes. The Bond Tax will replace the City's existing 0.625% sales and use tax levied in 2018 for the purpose of retiring bonds to finance water improvements (the "2018 Tax"). The effective date of the Bond Tax will be the day following the date that the 2018 Tax expires. Proceeds of the bonds may fund a debt service reserve and pay expenses of issuing the bonds. The bonds may be issued at one time or in series from time to time.

place: Northeast Benton County Emergency Medical Service District
title: Special Referendum Election
text: Ordinance No. O-2026-36 adopted by the Benton County Quorum Court increasing the annual service fee for each household within the EMSD area from $100.00 per household to a 4% increase annually for ten years beginning January 1, 2027 and ending January 1, 2037 per household conditioned on approval of such increase by the qualified voters of the EMSD area at a referendum election. FOR increasing the service fee for EMSD from $100.00 per household to a 4% increase annually for ten years beginning January 1, 2027 and ending January 1, 2037 per household. AGAINST increasing the service fee for EMSD from $100.00 per household to a 4% increase annually for ten years beginning January 1, 2027 and ending January 1, 2037 per household.

place: Northeast Benton County Volunteer Fire Department
title: Levy of Dues
text: If the levy of the volunteer fire department dues is approved, the dues shall be listed annually on real property tax statements and collected at the same time and in the same manner as real property taxes. FOR the levy of annual dues on each residence and on each business having an occupiable structure located in the designated area of the Northeast Benton County Volunteer Fire Department based on the following with a 4% increase beginning January 1, 2027 and increasing 4% each year for 10 years, ending January 1, 2037. Appraised Value Annual Dues $0 - 99,999 $84 $100,000 - 299,999 $154 $300,000 - or more $244 AGAINST the levy of annual dues on each residence and on each business having an occupiable structure located in the designated area of the Northeast Benton County Volunteer Fire Department based on the following with a 4% increase beginning January 1, 2027 and increasing 4% each year for 10 years, ending January 1, 2037. Appraised Value Annual Dues $0 - 99,999 $84 $100,000 - 299,999 $154 $300,000 - or more $244

title: County jails: transaction privilege tax of one-fifth of one cent (wording from the Board resolution, Section 3B; the printed ballot text may differ)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: COUNTY JAILS: TRANSACTION PRIVILEGE TAX OF ONE-FIFTH OF ONE CENT, the same rate as the existing jail facilities excise tax expiring in March 2027. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: Pursuant to authority granted by the State of Arizona, the County seeks voter approval of a transaction privilege tax set at the rate allowed under A.R.S. § 42-6109.02, section A, one-fifth of one cent to be used for county jail facilities and programs. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of approving a sales tax of one-fifth of one cent ($0.002) for county jail facilities and programs, the same rate as the current tax that is expiring. A “no” vote shall have the effect of rejecting a sales tax of one-fifth of one cent ($0.002) for jail facilities and programs.

title: Franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A MEASURE REFERRED TO THE PEOPLE BY THE CASA GRANDE CITY COUNCIL RELATING TO A FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR THE USE OF THE PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY IN THE CITY OF CASA GRANDE, ARIZONA FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ITS ELECTRIC UTILITY DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: SHALL A FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY BE APPROVED FOR A PERIOD OF 25 YEARS FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ITS ELECTRIC UTILITY WITHIN THE CITY RIGHTS-OF-WAY, IN THE FORM PROVIDED TO THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF CASA GRANDE. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of approving a franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company to allow them to use the City-owned public rights-of-way to construct, operate, and maintain its electric utility within the City of Casa Grande. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not approving a franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company to allow them to use the City-owned public rights-of-way to construct, operate, and maintain its electric utility within the City of Casa Grande.

title: Franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: SHALL A FRANCHISE BE GRANTED TO ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY, AN ARIZONA CORPORATION; TO CONSTRUCT, MAINTAIN AND OPERATE AN ELECTRIC UTILITY SYSTEM IN THE CITY OF ELOY, ARIZONA, AND FUTURE ADDITIONS THERETO, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE AGREEMENT SUBMITTED BY THE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ELOY, ARIZONA, TO THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF SAID CITY? DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: CONSIDERATION OF A FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR A PERIOD OF 25 YEARS FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ITS ELECTRIC UTILITY WITHIN THE CITY. A "yes" vote shall have the effect of approving a franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company to use the City-owned public rights-of-way to construct, operate, and maintain its electric utility within said City. A "no" vote shall have the effect of not approving a franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company to use the City-owned public rights-of-way to construct, operate, and maintain its electric utility within said City.

title: Eloy General Plan ratification
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: SHALL “ELOY GENERAL PLAN: PLANNING TODAY FOR A STRONGER TOMORROW”, AND ALL OF ITS ELEMENTS, BE RATIFIED AND APPROVED AS THE GENERAL PLAN FOR THE CITY OF ELOY? DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PROPOSAL TO THE VOTERS FOR RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF ELOY GENERAL PLAN: PLANNING TODAY FOR A STRONGER TOMORROW, AS ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL ON JUNE 2, 2026, RESOLUTION NO. 26-1660 THE GENERAL PLAN IS A STATEMENT OF LAND DEVELOPMENT POLICIES THAT SETS FORTH OBJECTIVES, PRINCIPLES AND STANDARDS FOR GROWTH AND REDEVELOPMENT. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of ratifying and approving the “Eloy General Plan – Planning Today for a Stronger Tomorrow”, and all of its elements as adopted by the City Council of the City of Eloy, Arizona, as the General Plan for the City of Eloy and shall become effective as provided by law. A “no” vote shall have the effect of keeping the current “City of Eloy General Plan Readoption, May 11, 2020”, in effect until a new General Plan is presented, ratified, and approved by the Eloy City Council and the voters of the City of Eloy, Arizona, as provided by law.

title: Extension of alternative expenditure limitation (sample shows official and descriptive titles only, with no question sentence)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A RESOLUTION PROPOSING AN EXTENSION OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE TOWN OF KEARNY. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PURSUANT TO THE ARIZONA STATE CONSTITUTION, THIS PROPOSAL ESTABLISHED AN EXTENSION OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE TOWN OF KEARNY FOR THE NEXT FOUR YEARS. ANNUALLY, THE TOWN COUNCIL WILL DETERMINE THE AMOUNT OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE FISCAL YEAR AFTER AT LEAST ONE PUBLIC HEARING. THIS ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION REPLACES THE STATE-IMPOSED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of extending the alternative expenditure limitation for the Town of Kearny. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not allowing the Town of Kearny to extend the alternative expenditure limitation and to require expenditures of the city to be limited by the state-imposed expenditure formula.

title: Permanent base expenditure limitation adjustment
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A RESOLUTION PROPOSING A PERMANENT BASE ADJUSTMENT TO THE 1979-80 STATE IMPOSED BASE LIMITATION FOR THE TOWN OF SAN TAN VALLEY. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PURSUANT TO THE ARIZONA STATE CONSTITUTION, THIS PROPOSAL PERMANENTLY ADJUSTS THE TOWN OF SAN TAN VALLEY’S 1979-80 BASE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION BY $183,997,957 IN FISCAL YEAR 2028, INCREASING THE TOWN’S ESTIMATED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION TO $850,000,000. THIS PERMANENT BASE ADJUSTMENT MODIFIES THE STATE-IMPOSED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION AND DOES NOT CHANGE THE PROPERTY TAX OR SALES TAX. SHALL THE TOWN OF SAN TAN VALLEY, ARIZONA, PERMANENTLY ADJUST ITS 1979-80 BASE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION BY $183,997,957 BEGINNING IN FISCAL YEAR 2028? A “yes” vote shall have the effect of permanently adjusting the Town of San Tan Valley’s 1979-80 base expenditure limitation by $183,997,957, in fiscal year 2028, increasing the Town’s base expenditure limitation to $850,000,000, which will then continue to grow annually based on population and inflation. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not allowing the Town of San Tan Valley to adjust its base adjustment limit, and the Town continue to be subject to the existing state-imposed expenditure limitation and may be legally prohibited from spending the revenues it receives and appropriates through the annual budget process.

title: Extension of alternative expenditure limitation (sample shows official and descriptive titles only, with no question sentence)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A RESOLUTION PROPOSING AN EXTENSION OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE CITY OF COOLIDGE. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PURSUANT TO THE ARIZONA STATE CONSTITUTION, THIS PROPOSAL ESTABLISHES AN EXTENSION OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE CITY OF COOLIDGE FOR THE NEXT FOUR YEARS. ANNUALLY, THE CITY COUNCIL WILL DETERMINE THE AMOUNT OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE FISCAL YEAR AFTER AT LEAST ONE PUBLIC HEARING. THIS ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION REPLACES THE STATE-IMPOSED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of extending the alternative expenditure limitation for the City of Coolidge. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not allowing the City of Coolidge to extend the alternative expenditure limitation and to require expenditures of the city to be limited by the state-imposed expenditure formula.

title: Franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A MEASURE SUBMITTED TO THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF THE TOWN OF FLORENCE BY THE FLORENCE TOWN COUNCIL RELATING TO THE PROPOSED GRANT OF A NONEXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR THE USE OF PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY WITHIN THE TOWN OF FLORENCE, ARIZONA, FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ELECTRIC UTILITY FACILITIES. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: CONSIDERATION OF A PROPOSED NONEXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR A TERM OF 25 YEARS ALLOWING USE OF PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY WITHIN THE TOWN OF FLORENCE TO CONSTRUCT, OPERATE, AND MAINTAIN ELECTRIC UTILITY FACILITIES. Shall a nonexclusive franchise be granted to Arizona Public Service Company, in the form of the proposed franchise agreement filed with the Town Clerk and published as required by law, for a term of 25 years, authorizing Arizona Public Service Company to use public rights-of-way within the Town of Florence to construct, operate, and maintain electric utility facilities? A “yes” vote shall have the effect of approving the grant of a nonexclusive franchise agreement to Arizona Public Service Company, in the form filed and published, authorizing Arizona Public Service Company to use public rights-of-way within the Town of Florence for a 25-year term to construct, operate, and maintain electric utility facilities. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not approving the grant of the proposed nonexclusive franchise agreement to Arizona Public Service Company for the use of public rights-of-way within the Town of Florence.

title: Maricopa General Plan ratification (“Advancing Maricopa”)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PROPOSED RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN, PURSUANT TO A.R.S. § 9-461.06, AS SET FORTH IN RESOLUTION 26-10 ADOPTING “ADVANCING MARICOPA,” THE CITY OF MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN AND LAND USE MAP, APPROVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA ON JUNE 2, 2026. THE GENERAL PLAN PROVIDES DIRECTION FOR DEVELOPMENT, CONSERVATION AND INFRASTRUCTURE INVESTMENTS IN THE CITY. IT DOES NOT CHANGE ANY CURRENT ZONING OR RAISE ANY TAXES. SHALL “ADVANCING MARICOPA,” THE MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN AND LAND USE MAP, AS ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL ON THE 2ND DAY OF JUNE 2026, BE APPROVED BY THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA. A yes vote shall have the effect of approving “Advancing Maricopa,” the Maricopa General Plan and Land Use Map as adopted by the City Council and it shall become effective as provided by law. A no vote shall have the effect of leaving the Maricopa 2016 General Plan in place until such time as Council shall adopt other provisions which may be ratified by the voters.

title: $39,000,000 general obligation bonds
text: SHALL COOLIDGE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 21 OF PINAL COUNTY, ARIZONA (THE “DISTRICT”), BE ALLOWED TO ISSUE AND SELL GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS IN THE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF NOT TO EXCEED $39,000,000 TO PROVIDE MONEY FOR THE FOLLOWING PURPOSES: • CONSTRUCTING AND/OR PURCHASING SCHOOL BUILDINGS; • RENOVATING SCHOOL BUILDINGS; • PURCHASING PUPIL TRANSPORTATION VEHICLES; • ACQUIRING BY PURCHASE OR LEASE SCHOOL LOTS; • IMPROVING SCHOOL GROUNDS, INCLUDING ADJACENT WAYS THERETO; • SUPPLYING SCHOOL BUILDINGS WITH FURNITURE, EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY; • LIQUIDATING INDEBTEDNESS INCURRED FOR THE PURPOSES SET FORTH HEREIN; • PROVIDING ALL UTILITIES AND OTHER CAPITAL ITEMS NECESSARY FOR THE CONSTRUCTION AND RENOVATION OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS AND FOR IMPROVING SCHOOL GROUNDS; • PAYING ALL ARCHITECTURAL, DESIGN, ENGINEERING, PROJECT AND CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND OTHER COSTS INCURRED IN CONNECTION WITH THE PURPOSES SET FORTH ABOVE; AND • PAYING ALL LEGAL, FINANCIAL AND OTHER COSTS IN CONNECTION WITH ISSUANCE OF THE BONDS? THE BONDS WILL BEAR INTEREST AT RATES NOT EXCEEDING 12% PER YEAR. INTEREST MAY BE EVIDENCED BY SEPARATE CERTIFICATES AND WILL BE PAID ON JANUARY 1 AND JULY 1 EACH YEAR UNTIL THE BONDS MATURE. THE BONDS, AND ANY BONDS ISSUED TO REFUND THE DISTRICT’S BONDS, MAY BE SOLD AT PRICES THAT INCLUDE PREMIUMS NOT GREATER THAN PERMITTED BY LAW. THE BONDS MAY BE REFUNDED BY THE ISSUANCE OF REFUNDING BONDS OF A WEIGHTED AVERAGE MATURITY OF LESS THAN 75% OF THE WEIGHTED AVERAGE MATURITY OF THE BONDS BEING REFUNDED. BONDS WILL BE IN THE DENOMINATIONS OF $5,000 EACH OR IN MULTIPLES OF $5,000 AND WILL MATURE ON THE FIRST DAY OF JANUARY AND/OR JULY IN YEARS DETERMINED BY THE DISTRICT’S GOVERNING BOARD. THE BONDS SHALL MATURE OVER A PERIOD OF NOT (I) LESS THAN ONE (1) YEAR (OR A PORTION THEREOF) OR (II) MORE THAN TWENTY (20) YEARS FROM THE DATE OF THEIR ISSUANCE. THE ISSUANCE OF THESE BONDS WILL RESULT IN A PROPERTY TAX INCREASE SUFFICIENT TO PAY THE ANNUAL DEBT SERVICE ON BONDS. THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS THAT ARE PROPOSED TO BE FUNDED THROUGH THIS BOND ISSUANCE ARE TO EXCEED THE STATE STANDARDS AND ARE IN ADDITION TO MONIES PROVIDED BY THE STATE. COOLIDGE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 21 IS PROPOSING TO ISSUE CLASS B GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS TOTALING $39,000,000 TO FUND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS OVER AND ABOVE THOSE FUNDED BY THE STATE. UNDER THE STUDENTS FIRST CAPITAL FUNDING SYSTEM, COOLIDGE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 21 IS ENTITLED TO STATE MONIES FOR NEW CONSTRUCTION AND RENOVATION OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS IN ACCORDANCE WITH STATE LAW. A “yes” vote shall authorize the Coolidge Unified School District No. 21 of Pinal County, Arizona governing body to issue and sell $39,000,000 of school improvement bonds of the district to be repaid with secondary property taxes. A “no” vote shall not authorize the Coolidge Unified School District No. 21 of Pinal County, Arizona governing body to issue and sell such bonds of the district.

title: Maintenance and operation budget override continuation
text: SHALL THE GOVERNING BOARD OF MARICOPA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 20 OF PINAL COUNTY, ARIZONA (THE “DISTRICT”), ADOPT A GENERAL MAINTENANCE AND OPERATION BUDGET THAT INCLUDES AN AMOUNT THAT EXCEEDS THE REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT SPECIFIED BY STATUTE BY 10% FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028 AND FOR SIX (6) SUBSEQUENT YEARS AS DESCRIBED BELOW? THE FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028 BUDGET OVERRIDE AUTHORITY REPRESENTS AN EXTENSION OF THE EXISTING BUDGET OVERRIDE AUTHORITY WHICH IS SCHEDULED TO PHASE DOWN BY ONE-THIRD FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028, BY ANOTHER ONE-THIRD FOR FISCAL YEAR 2028/2029, AND WILL TERMINATE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2029/2030 IF THE VOTERS DO NOT APPROVE THE OVERRIDE. THE AMOUNT OF THE PROPOSED CONTINUATION OF THE BUDGET INCREASE OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET OVER THE ALTERNATE BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028 IS ESTIMATED TO BE $2,758,048. IN FISCAL YEARS 2027/2028 THROUGH 2031/2032 THE AMOUNT OF THE PROPOSED INCREASE WILL BE 10% OF THE DISTRICT’S REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT IN EACH OF SUCH YEARS, AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 15-481(P) OF THE ARIZONA REVISED STATUTES. IN FISCAL YEARS 2032/2033 AND 2033/2034, THE AMOUNT OF THE PROPOSED INCREASE WILL BE 6.67% AND 3.33%, RESPECTIVELY, OF THE DISTRICT’S REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT IN EACH OF SUCH YEARS, AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 15-481(P) OF THE ARIZONA REVISED STATUTES. ANY BUDGET INCREASE CONTINUATION AUTHORIZED BY THIS ELECTION SHALL BE ENTIRELY FUNDED BY A LEVY OF TAXES ON THE TAXABLE PROPERTY IN THIS SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR THE YEAR FOR WHICH ADOPTED AND FOR SIX (6) SUBSEQUENT YEARS, SHALL NOT BE REALIZED FROM MONIES FURNISHED BY THE STATE AND SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATION ON TAXES SPECIFIED IN ARTICLE IX, SECTION 18, CONSTITUTION OF ARIZONA. BASED ON THE CURRENT NET ASSESSED VALUATION USED FOR SECONDARY PROPERTY TAX PURPOSES, TO FUND THE PROPOSED CONTINUATION OF THE INCREASE IN THE SCHOOL DISTRICT’S BUDGET WOULD REQUIRE AN ESTIMATED CONTINUATION OF A TAX RATE OF $1.39 PER ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS OF ASSESSED VALUATION USED FOR SECONDARY PROPERTY TAX PURPOSES AND IS IN ADDITION TO THE SCHOOL DISTRICT’S TAX RATE THAT WILL BE LEVIED TO FUND THE SCHOOL DISTRICT’S REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT ALLOWED BY LAW. A “yes” vote shall authorize the Maricopa Unified School District No. 20 School District Governing Board to continue the existing maintenance and operation budget override authority and resulting tax, which includes an amount that exceeds the District’s revenue control limit. A “no” vote shall not authorize the Maricopa Unified School District No. 20 School District Governing Board to extend the existing maintenance and operation budget override authority and resulting tax.

title: Sports Arena Facility Financing Assistance Act
text: Shall the City of Lincoln, Nebraska establish a volleyball sports complex economic development project as described above by appropriating annually from state assistance received by the City pursuant to the Sports Arena Facility Financing Assistance Act?

title: Charter Amendment changing city election date
text: SHALL ARTICLES III AND IV OF THE LINCOLN CITY CHARTER BE AMENDED TO ALIGN CITY ELECTIONS WITH STATEWIDE ELECTIONS BEGINNING IN 2028 SO THAT MAYORAL AND DISTRICT COUNCIL MEMBER ELECTIONS ARE HELD IN BOTH 2027 AND 2028; AND THAT AT-LARGE COUNCIL MEMBERS ELECTED IN 2025 SHALL SERVE UNTIL THEIR SUCCESSORS ARE ELECTED IN 2030; AND THAT ELECTED TERMS OF A LENGTH DIFFERENT THAN FOUR-YEARS DUE TO THIS PROVISION SHALL COUNT AS A FOUR-YEAR TERM FOR PURPOSES OF TERM LIMITS?

title: Alternative Charter Amendment changing city election date
text: CITY'S ALTERNATIVE AMENDMENT: SHALL ARTICLES III AND IV OF THE LINCOLN CITY CHARTER BE AMENDED TO ALIGN CITY ELECTIONS WITH STATEWIDE ELECTIONS BEGINNING IN 2030 SO THAT MAYORAL AND DISTRICT COUNCIL MEMBER ELECTIONS ARE HELD IN BOTH 2027 AND 2030; AND THAT AT-LARGE COUNCIL MEMBER ELECTIONS ARE HELD IN BOTH 2029 AND 2032; AND THAT ELECTED TERMS OF A LENGTH DIFFERENT THAN FOUR-YEARS DUE TO THIS PROVISION SHALL COUNT AS A FOUR-YEAR TERM FOR PURPOSES OF TERM LIMITS?

title: Charter Amendment imposing city council term limits
text: SHALL ARTICLE III, SECTION 4 OF THE CHARTER BE AMENDED TO PROVIDE THAT COUNCIL MEMBERS SHALL NOT BE QUALIFIED TO HOLD OFFICE FOR MORE THAN TWO CONSECUTIVE FOUR-YEAR TERMS?

title: Alternative Charter Amendment imposing city council term limits
text: CITY'S ALTERNATIVE AMENDMENT: SHALL ARTICLE III, SECTION 4 OF THE CHARTER BE AMENDED TO PROVIDE THAT COUNCIL MEMBERS SHALL NOT BE QUALIFIED TO HOLD OFFICE FOR MORE THAN THREE CONSECUTIVE FOUR-YEAR TERMS?

title: Charter Amendment allowing residents outside city corporate limits to vote in city elections
text: SHALL ARTICLE III, SECTION 2 AND ARTICLE IV, SECTION 2A OF THE CHARTER BE AMENDED TO ALLOW ALL CITIZENS RESIDING IN THE THREE-MILE EXTRATERRITORIAL ZONING JURISDICTION AROUND THE CITY, BUT NOT WITHIN THE CITY'S CORPORATE LIMITS, TO VOTE IN ITS ELECTIONS?

title: School Bond Election
text: Shall Freeman School District in the State of Nebraska issue its bonds in a total principal amount not to exceed $13,995,000 for the purposes of financing the costs of (a) constructing a new building on the District's existing campus that will include career and trades education and additional classroom areas, (b) renovating portions of the existing school building, including the expansion of the current kitchen and repurposing certain classrooms and areas in connection with the construction of the new building, and (c) purchasing certain necessary equipment, furniture and apparatus for such new building and renovations, and making related site improvements; said bonds to be issued from time to time, to be sold at such prices, to bear interest at such rates, to become due at such times, and to have such other terms and provisions, all as may be fixed and determined by the Board of Education of the District; and "Shall the District cause to be levied and collected annually a special levy of taxes against all the taxable property in the District sufficient in rate and amount to pay the principal of, the premium, if any, and the interest on said bonds as the same become due?"

title: Sales and Use Tax
text: Shall the governing body of the Village of Raymond, Lancaster County, Nebraska impose a sales and use tax upon the same transactions within the municipality on which the State of Nebraska is authorized to impose a tax, specifically, impose a tax of one and one-half percent (1.5%) for village capital and infrastructure improvements including streets, utilities, parks, landscaping, beautification and tree planting.

title: Village of Sprague Sales and Use Tax
text: The Village of Sprague, Nebraska proposes to impose a sales and use tax in the amount of one and one-half percent (1.5%) upon certain transactions within the Village on which the State of Nebraska and Village of Sprague are authorized to impose pursuant to the Nebraska Local Option Revenue Act. Shall the governing body of the incorporated municipality impose a sales and use tax in the amount of 1.5% upon the same transactions within such municipality on which the State of Nebraska is authorized to impose a tax?

title: Village of Denton Board of Trustees Recall
text: Shall Amanda Fangmeier be removed from the office of the Village of Denton Board of Trustees?

title: Special City of Omaha Election, $155,000,000 Public Facilities Bonds
text: Shall the City of Omaha be authorized to issue and sell general obligation bonds in the amount of one hundred fifty-five million and no/100 dollars ($155,000,000) for the purpose of providing funds for payment of the cost of acquiring, constructing, improving, equipping and rehabilitating police buildings and facilities, fire stations, branch libraries, park maintenance facilities, auditorium support facilities, arena and convention center facilities, public works storage facilities and city wide building renovations and replacements and other public facilities of the City of Omaha, the approximate cost to the taxpayers of the City of Omaha if this proposal is approved to be one hundred fifty-five million and no/100 dollars ($155,000,000) plus interest payable on said bonds to be paid from the fund for principal and interest payments on the indebtedness of the City of Omaha as proposed in the notice of election which also provides that the approval of this bond issue will not incur any increases in the debt services tax levy rate of the City of Omaha over the levy increase approved in 2020?

title: Special City of Omaha Election, $30,000,000 Park & Recreation Bonds
text: Shall the City of Omaha be authorized to issue and sell general obligation bonds in the amount of thirty million and no/100 dollars ($30,000,000) for the purpose of providing funds for payment of the cost of various park and recreation improvement projects of the City of Omaha, the approximate cost to the taxpayers of the City of Omaha if this proposal is approved to be thirty million and no/100 dollars ($30,000,000) plus interest payable on said bonds to be paid from the fund for principal and interest payments on the indebtedness of the City of Omaha as proposed in the notice of election which also provides that the approval of this bond issue will not incur any increases in the debt services tax levy rate of the City of Omaha over the levy increase approved in 2020?

title: Special City of Valley Election, Proposition for Sales and Use Tax Allocation
text: Shall the City Council of the City of Valley, Nebraska, be authorized to allocate up to fifty percent (50%) of the revenue the City collects from its one and one-half percent (1.5%) local sales and use tax, on and after January 1, 2027, for the purpose of planning, designing, constructing, equipping, financing, and maintaining a new municipal swimming pool and related aquatic facilities?

title: School Bond
text: Shall Doniphan-Trumbull Public Schs School District in the State of Nebraska issue its bonds in a total principal amount not to exceed $17,500,000 for the purposes of financing the costs of (a) making certain renovations and constructing one or more additions to the District's existing school building and related site improvements, and (b) purchasing certain equipment, furniture and apparatus for such school building and additions; said bonds to be issued from time to time, to be sold at such prices, to bear interest at such rates, to become due at such times, and to have such other terms and provisions, all as may be fixed and determined by the Board of Education of the District; and "Shall the District cause to be levied and collected annually a special levy of taxes against all the taxable property in the District sufficient in rate and amount to pay the principal of, the premium, if any, and the interest on said bonds as the same become due?"

title: Weed Board Dissolution
text: Shall the Hall County Weed District Board be dissolved and its duties and authority be exercised by the Hall County Board of Commissioners?

publisher: Charleston County Board of Voter Registration & Elections
title: Sales and Use Tax Referendum
text: I approve a special sales and use tax in the amount of one-half (1/2) of one percent to be imposed in Charleston County for not more than twenty-five (25) years, or until a total of $4,250,000,000 in resulting revenue has been collected, whichever occurs first. The sales tax proceeds will be used to fund the following projects: Project (1) $2,702,000,000 – For financing the costs of highways, roads, streets, bridges, and other transportation-related projects facilities, and drainage facilities related thereto, that include: Featured Projects: Rivers Avenue Railroad Overpass at Durant Avenue, Mall Drive (S-790) Improvements, Patriot Boulevard Widening, Better North Bridge Pedestrian and Bicycle Improvements, Battery Extension West / Calhoun Street - Medical District, Hagood Avenue Improvements, Maybank Highway Southern Pitchfork and Roundabouts, Glenn McConnell Parkway at Magwood Road, US 17 South Widening from Dobbin Road to SC-162, Johnnie Dodds Boulevard at Houston Northcutt Boulevard and Wingo Way Improvements, Long Point Road Resiliency and Safety Improvements. Intersection Projects: Stall Road at Midland Park Road and Ashley Phosphate Road, Ladson Road at Palmetto Commerce Parkway, Ashley Phosphate Road at Cross County Road and Brandywine Road, US 78 at Limehouse Lane, Savannah Highway at Ashley Town Center Drive, Maybank Highway at Riverland Drive, Main Road at Mary Ann Point Roundabout, SC-162 at Salters Hill Roundabout, SC-174 at SC-164 Roundabout, Steed Creek Road at US 17 North, SC-45 at US 17 North. Whipple Road at Mathis Ferry Road and Lucy Beckham High School. Pavement Management: Resurfacing paved roads throughout Charleston County based on condition, traffic volume, safety requirements, and age of infrastructure, Rural Road Safety Program, Roadway Elevation Resiliency Program including Seabrook Island Road Project. Bike / Pedestrian Improvements: Bike and Pedestrian infrastructure throughout Charleston County, including but not limited to, Countywide Bike Ped Plan, Rivers Avenue Lowcountry Rapid Transit Last Mile Connections, City of Charleston Safe Streets for All Plan, Rethink Folly Road Plan, Mount Pleasant Way Plan. Other Projects: 2016 Sales and Use Tax Carryover Projects (Dorchester Road Widening and Palmetto Commerce Parkway Phase 3), Traffic Signal Synchronization, Reynolds Avenue Improvements, Noise Wall at Palmetto Commerce Interchange Project, and other future needs for highways, roads, streets, bridges, and drainage facilities. All featured projects, intersection projects, pavement management projects, and all other projects shall consider the inclusion of bicycle, pedestrian, and public transit access in the design process, as contextually appropriate. If any project listed above cannot be accomplished, the amounts of Sales and Use Tax associated will be applied to any other project listed above Project (2) $858,000,000 – For financing the operation and expansion of public transit systems operated by Charleston Area Regional Transportation Authority (CARTA) or jointly operated by the County and other governmental entities and the implementation of the Downtown Route Study. Project (3) $690,000,000 – For financing the costs of greenbelts with a 50% urban and 50% rural allocation of the revenues, including but not limited to, purchasing land for conservation, conservation easements, passive greenspaces, public parks, access points to waterways; and protecting natural resources, agricultural landscapes, heritage landscapes, scenic corridors and water resources.

publisher: Charleston County Board of Voter Registration & Elections
title: General Obligation Bonds Referendum
text: I approve the issuance of not exceeding $300,000,000 of general obligation bonds of Charleston County, payable from the special sales and use tax described in Question 1 above, maturing over a period not to exceed twenty-five (25) years, to fund completion of projects from among the categories described in Question 1 above.

title: Homestead Exemption ($50,000)
text: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Butts County ad valorem taxes for county purposes in the amount of $50,000.00 of the assessed value of the homestead for residents of that county?

title: Homestead Exemption ($70,000, Age 62 or Older)
text: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Butts County ad valorem taxes for county purposes in the amount of $70,000.00 of the assessed value of the homestead for residents of that county who are 62 years of age or older?”

title: Local Option Sales Tax Referendum
text: Must a one percent (1%) sales and use tax be levied in Georgetown County for the purpose of allowing a credit against a taxpayer's county and municipal ad valorem tax liability and for the purpose of funding county and municipal operations in the Georgetown County area?

publisher: Spalding County Board of Elections and Registration
title: County 1% Sales and Use Tax
text: Shall a special one percent sales and use tax be imposed in Spalding County for a period of time not to exceed 24 calendar quarters and for the raising of an estimated amount of $134,000,000 for the purpose of funding the following capital outlay projects: (i) for Spalding County (A) transportation projects to include roads, streets, bridges, sidewalks, and trails, (B) County park deferred maintenance, (C) a new facility for E911 and acquisition of NextGen 911 software, (D) debt reduction for fire truck engines and ladder trucks for the Fire Department, (E) building maintenance renovations and update for Public Works, (F) County annex renovations, (G) elections office renovations, (H) collection centers and equipment and vehicles for Solid Waste, (I) sewer improvements and expansion for economic development, (J) maintenance shop update and new fueling station for county fleet and (K) equipment and vehicles for Storm Water Department; (ii) for the City of Griffin (A) acquisition and construction of new fire stations, including fire station equipment, (B) public safety equipment, (C) nuisance abatement for community development, and (D) transportation projects to include roads, streets, bridges, sidewalks, and parking; (iii) and for Orchard Hill, (A) improvements to City parks including a walking track, pickleball courts, and shades for playground equipment, (B) acquisition of new City property, and (C) inter-City improvements? If imposition of the tax is approved by the voters, such vote shall also constitute approval of the issuance of general obligation debt of the City of Griffin in a principal amount not to exceed $20,000,000 for a portion of the above described capital outlay projects of the City of Griffin.
